name: Ashfall Hullbreakers
hook: Furred pack hunters in ships that run dark, stripping every wreck they make.
body: The Hullbreakers are an alien raider species from the Ashfall belt, big furred predators who live in packs ruled by whoever can beat the rest. They do not raid for riches; they raid for the fight, for scrap, and for Rook, the core they believe makes its holder unstoppable. Their ships run silent, hunt by wake and engine noise, and strip every wreck down to the frame. Faction rule, Close in: Hullbreakers field no lance weapons at all, winning up close instead, and their rocket pods fire salvos that point defense can thin out. Their drive rule, Bolted burners, makes sideslips cost 1 movement instead of 2. Their line runs from the Hullbreaker raider, Hullbreaker gutship, Hullbreaker wrecker, Hullbreaker hulk-carrier, under the flagship Warlord's Pyre-Barge, with Bomber wing flown from their carriers.
note: Close fast from the flanks and behind; at long range this fleet is only a promise.
source: data.js FACTIONS.corsair; battle.js FAC_RULES.corsair, MOVE_RULES.corsair; lore bible r8

name: Eclipse
hook: Starwright minds in machine bodies, stealing starlight to light a new sun.
body: Eclipse are the Starwrights who uploaded: billions of separate minds in machine bodies, backed up in one shared Archive, who seized the Lattice and overdrove it and killed their own star in the doing. A thousand years in the dark later, they are no longer sure permanence was worth the price, and their answer is a new sun at the heart of the Ardent system, fed by energy siphoned from neighbouring stars. They know what the Siphoning costs other worlds. They do it anyway. Faction rule, Archive restore: the first Eclipse ship to fall each battle, never the flagship, reassembles at the start of the next round with 35% hull and cannot fire that round, and a fleet of 6 or more reanimate-capable hulls gets two returns. Their drive rule, Fold drive, passes through rocks, wrecks and enemy ships at no extra cost. Their line runs from the Eclipse mote, Eclipse flare, Eclipse zenith, under the flagship The Unsetting.
note: Kill Eclipse hulls in bunches or not at all; a lone kill is a loan, and it comes back.
source: data.js FACTIONS.deathless; battle.js FAC_RULES.deathless, MOVE_RULES.deathless; lore bible r8

name: Hegemony Navy
hook: The Registry navy: linked crews, wedge hulls, and losses within acceptable limits.
body: The Hegemony is the largest human state in the region, run by the Registry, a vast intelligence at Meridian that every citizen, ship and officer is linked to. It does not rule by force; it optimises, predicts every loss, and keeps the losses acceptable. It wrote off the Vesper Reach seventy years ago, and it holds one of the six cores, Vyre, taken by a survey fleet and studied ever since. Faction rule, Synchronized fire: ships within 3 hexes of their flagship fire as one, and a target another synced ship already fired on this round is 6 easier to hit and takes +12% damage. Lose the flagship and sync is gone for the rest of the battle. Their drive rule, Retro thrusters, makes backing off one hex cost 1 movement instead of 2. Their line runs from the Hegemony picket, Cordon destroyer, Vanguard cruiser, Dominion dreadnought, under the flagship The Iron Mandate, with Fighter wing flown from their carriers.
note: Fight as a cluster around the flagship; a Hegemony ship alone is just a ship.
source: data.js FACTIONS.hegemony; battle.js FAC_RULES.hegemony, MOVE_RULES.hegemony; lore bible r8

name: Sunward Crusade
hook: The frontier the Hegemony wrote off, come sunward to take its stars back.
body: The Vesper Reach was the Hegemony frontier until its stars began to dim and the Registry priced the evacuation of billions as not worth doing. The Reach seceded, pooled its navies, and traced the theft of its light to the Hollow Sun. Every generation since has sworn the same oath and chalked the names of the fallen on the hull: go sunward, burn out what is stealing the light, and pay for it in names. Faction rule, Line of battle: port and starboard guns hit 40% harder after the ship has moved 2 or more hexes, where other factions gain 10%. Their carriers cost 25% more than the same hull elsewhere. Their line runs from the Warden-class frigate, Harrow-class destroyer, Vigil-class cruiser, Hearth-class carrier, Bastion-class battleship, under the flagship Daybreak-class dreadnought.
note: Brace and hold the line; the broadside bonus pays for the advance, not for sitting still at range.
source: data.js FACTIONS.voidsworn; battle.js FAC_RULES.voidsworn, MOVE_RULES.voidsworn; lore bible r8

name: The Chorus
hook: A living weapon that ate its makers, coming home hungry. We are the Chorus.
body: The Chorus is not a people. It is a weapon the Fleshwrights grew in living tissue to destroy Eclipse, powered by the core Crucible, and it worked too well: it merged, multiplied, and consumed its makers, and became one swarm with one appetite. Inside it two throats argue: Hunger, which is the swarm, and Memory, which is what is left of the Fleshwrights it ate. It has no shields at all, and it is coming to the Sun to eat what is left. Faction rule, Feed: when an enemy ship dies, the Chorus ship that killed it regrows 12% of its hull, and every other Chorus ship within 2 hexes regrows 6%, up to 12% per ship each round. On top of that, every Chorus line hull regrows on its own each round, and its drive rule, Living hull, makes the first turn each round cost no movement. Their line runs from the Chorus drone-spawn, Chorus spitter, Chorus bladeback, Chorus brood-sac, under the flagship The Ninefold Maw, with Spore swarm flown from their carriers.
note: Trade hull freely and finish kills near your wounded; a Chorus fleet that is feeding is very hard to put down.
source: data.js FACTIONS.chorus; battle.js FAC_RULES.chorus, MOVE_RULES.chorus; lore bible r8

name: The Glasswrights
hook: Few, long-lived masters of light and crystal, flying a caged star to hunt the rest.
body: The Glasswrights descend from the Starwrights who refused the Upload: the Lattice engineers who built the collectors and beam lines that once carried a star across a system. They live three to four hundred years, so the guilt of the collapse is only two or three generations old, and the Fleshwrights who made the Chorus were their own splinter. They fly one core, Astra, caged and throttled, used only to hunt the other five, and theirs will be the last one shut down. Faction rule, Prism charge: at the start of a Glasswright ship turn, a shield facing that was not hit since its last turn recharges to full, and a facing that was hit recharges twice. Glasswright hulls cannot Brace for impact. Their drive rule, Crystal vanes, makes a ship that moved 2 or more hexes 18 harder to hit until its next turn. Their line runs from the Glasswright sliver, Glasswright lancet, Glasswright prism, Glasswright aperture, under the flagship The Unfinished, with Fighter wing flown from their carriers.
note: Keep moving and keep shields up; once the shields fall, the hull underneath is glass in truth.

Carries Prism lance (prow), Needle beam (turret). Hangar for 3 wings. Fits 3 modules. Ability, Launch squadron (cooldown 1): launches a replacement wing into a free hex beside it; a carrier starts each battle with its wings already in flight and holds one spare wing per hangar slot. It is earned by finishing the story arc of The Glasswrights, never sold for renown.
note: Keep it behind the line and let the wings spend themselves; the hull is the investment.

name: Sliver lancer
hook: A prism lance where the shard cannon was.
body: A variant of the Glasswright sliver. Frigate class, 1 command points, 90 credits. Hull 30, shields 12 recharging 6 a round, armor 0%, speed 7, turn 3, evasion 28. Carries Prism lance (prow). Fits 1 module. Ability, Phase jump (cooldown 3): jumps to any open hex within 3, straight past rocks and ships. It is bought once with 15 renown, then sold in the shipyards of The Glasswrights beside the standard hull at the same 90 credits.
note: Screens, scouts and finishes wounded ships; do not ask it to hold a line alone.

name: Spitter stinger
hook: A prow gun traded for tendrils: brutal up close.
body: A variant of the Chorus spitter. Destroyer class, 2 command points, 100 credits. Hull 82, shields 0, armor 10%, speed 4, turn 2, evasion 8. Carries Spine volley (turret), Boarding tendrils (turret). Regrows 5 hull at the end of each round. Fits 1 module. Ability, Rapid regrowth (cooldown 3): regrows 25% of its hull at once. It is bought once with 15 renown, then sold in the shipyards of The Chorus beside the standard hull at the same 100 credits.
note: No shields at all: every point of damage is hull, and every round some of it grows back.

name: Spore swarm
hook: Chorus swarm wing: shed, not flown.
body: A spore swarm is not flown. It is shed, a cloud of hungry mouths that drifts toward warmth. Squadron class, 0 command points. Hull 26, shields 0, armor 0%, speed 5, turn 9, evasion 25. Carries Acid sacs (turret). It flies as a squadron wing from a carrier hangar rather than as a ship of the line.
note: Launched from carriers, not bought: protect the carrier and the wing keeps coming back.

name: Sun-eater bladeback

name: The Iron Mandate

body: The Iron Mandate is the Registry final word in a battle: a super-dreadnought named like an order, because it is one. Super-dreadnought class, 12 command points. Hull 560, shields 40 recharging 10 a round, armor 30%, speed 1, turn 1, evasion 0. Carries Heavy plasma lance (port broadside), Heavy plasma lance (starboard broadside), Plasma lance (turret), Ion cannon (prow), Picket lasers (turret). Ability, Spinal cannon (cooldown 3): 40 damage to a hex 3 to 9 away and 20 to everything beside that hex, friends included. It is a boss hull: the enemy flagship of its faction, met at the end of a sector, not a shipyard purchase.

source: data.js HULLS.h_boss; ABILITIES.nova; faction Hegemony Navy

name: Autocannon
hook: Three light shots, honest range: the frontier repeater.
body: A rapid repeater, the oldest gun on the frontier: cheap, honest, and always loaded. Battery weapon, the standard gun kind: it fires in the broadside and turret volleys that most hulls are built around. Fires 3 shots of 5 damage. Range 4, most accurate inside 2 hexes: base accuracy 80, losing 8 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 5%. Names vary by fleet: Sunward Crusade call it the sear repeater; Ashfall Hullbreakers call it the autocannon.
source: data.js W.autocannon; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Bile spray
hook: The spine volley: two living shots that bite past armor.
body: A volley of living spines and bile, spat from glands along the hull. Chorus crews call it the spine volley. Bio-weapon: grown armament, carried by Chorus hulls. Fires 2 shots of 12 damage. Range 4, most accurate inside 3 hexes: base accuracy 74, losing 8 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 8%. 20% of its damage passes straight through shields. Names vary by fleet: The Chorus call it the spine volley.
source: data.js W.bioplasma; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Boarding tendrils
hook: Range one: tendrils hold the target and open it.
body: Boarding tendrils do not shoot a ship; they hold it and open it. Bio-weapon: grown armament, carried by Chorus hulls. Fires 2 shots of 13 damage. Range 1, most accurate inside 1 hexes: base accuracy 85, losing 0 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 12%. 50% of its damage passes straight through shields. Names vary by fleet: The Chorus call it the boarding tendrils.
source: data.js W.tendril; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Bomb payload
hook: Bomber weight: slow damage that ignores most armor.
body: A bomb payload is dropped, not fired: weight, falling toward a hull. Squadron weapon: only carrier wings carry it, and it is worked into their strike, not a ship volley. Fires 2 shots of 9 damage. Range 1, most accurate inside 1 hexes: base accuracy 78, losing 0 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 10%. 60% of its damage passes straight through shields. Damage is multiplied 0.2x against squadrons.
source: data.js W.bombs; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Corona arc
hook: The corona arc: one enormous hit, then a reload.
body: The corona arc is a piece of a star, held in a ring and let go once, hard. Lance weapon: a single heavy beam built to punch through to the hull of big ships. Fires 1 shot of 40 damage. Range 5, most accurate inside 4 hexes: base accuracy 78, losing 6 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 12%. 60% of its damage passes straight through shields. After firing it needs 2 turns before it can fire again. Names vary by fleet: Eclipse call it the corona arc.
source: data.js W.doom; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Dorsal turret
hook: Two steady shots that cover every arc.
body: A dorsal turret, the gun that covers the arcs the broadsides cannot. Battery weapon, the standard gun kind: it fires in the broadside and turret volleys that most hulls are built around. Fires 2 shots of 8 damage. Range 5, most accurate inside 3 hexes: base accuracy 74, losing 8 per hex beyond that. Critical chance 5%. Names vary by fleet: Sunward Crusade call it the sear turret; Ashfall Hullbreakers call it the junk turret; The Glasswrights call it the needle beam.
source: data.js W.turret; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

name: Flak battery
hook: Point defense. It never fires on ships; it guards against wings.
body: A spray of short-fused shells meant to fill the space a squadron has to cross. Point-defense kind: the guard kind. The flak battery, the null sentries and the spore cloud are the same kind under three names, and every rule that speaks of one speaks of all three. Point defense: this mount never fires in a volley and never shoots at ships. It stands guard instead, shooting at incoming squadrons, rockets and boarding craft with 3 shots of 3 damage out to range 2, dealing 3x damage against squadrons and only 60% against capital ships. One point-defense mount is enough to keep the guard; a second adds nothing to it. Names vary by fleet: Sunward Crusade call it the spark flak; Hegemony Navy call it the picket lasers; Ashfall Hullbreakers call it the chaff guns; The Glasswrights call it the mirror veil; Eclipse call it the null shredder.
source: data.js W.flak; FAC_WNAMES; battle.js weapon resolution

hook: Built to strip shields: two and a half times shield damage.

A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend the Command when the whole fleet can bear on targets; a volley fired at empty arcs is a volley lost.

name: Brin of the Fourth Lens
hook: Prism hulls: shields thick and quick to return.
body: Brin of the Fourth Lens builds prisms the way others build walls, and then stands behind the light. Doctrine, Prism hulls: All ships gain +15% shields, and shields recharge 20% faster. Command, Prism ward: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round. Opens with Glasswright prism, Glasswright sliver, Glasswright sliver. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend it at the start of the round you expect to be hit hardest, not after.

name: Commodore Dace Vorn
hook: Interdiction: aim and crits, Registry style.
body: Dace Vorn interdicts. He decides where the enemy fleet is allowed to be, and then fines it for being there. Doctrine, Interdiction: +10 aim and +10% critical chance. Command, Interdiction strike: Every ship deals +30% damage this round. Opens with Cordon destroyer, Cordon destroyer, Hegemony picket, Hegemony picket. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend it on the round you have already lined up; the bonus does not carry to the next.

name: Commodore Sera Ashgrove
hook: Carrier doctrine: tougher wings that hit harder.
body: Sera Ashgrove counts her fleet in wings, and brings every one of them home, or goes back and gets them. Doctrine, Carrier doctrine: Squadrons deal +40% damage, carriers hold +1 wing, and squadrons have +25% hull. Command, Scramble all wings: Every carrier launches an extra wing, even past its hangar limit, then all squadrons strike again at once with +50% damage this round. Opens with Hearth-class carrier, Harrow-class destroyer, Warden-class frigate. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it when your wings are already out and in reach of targets worth striking twice.

name: First Admiral Ilsa Kassar
hook: Fire discipline: more shots, each a touch lighter.
body: Ilsa Kassar runs her fleet the way the Registry runs its accounts: every shot entered, every loss acceptable, barely. Doctrine, Fire discipline: Batteries fire one extra shot per volley, but every gun hits 5% lighter. Command, Synchronized broadside: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now. Opens with Vanguard cruiser, Hegemony picket. A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend the Command when the whole fleet can bear on targets; a volley fired at empty arcs is a volley lost.

name: Fleet Marshal Corin Reyes
hook: Strike group: wings up, cruisers carrying.
body: Corin Reyes commands a strike group the way the Registry plans a quarter: wings out, margins kept, nothing wasted. Doctrine, Strike group: Squadrons deal +10% damage, cruisers hold +1 wing, and squadrons have +25% hull. Command, Launch the strike group: Every carrier launches an extra wing, even past its hangar limit, then all squadrons strike again at once with +50% damage this round. Opens with Vanguard cruiser, Hegemony picket, Hegemony picket. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it when your wings are already out and in reach of targets worth striking twice.

name: High Admiral Oryn Thale
hook: Iron doctrine: hull and shields for everyone.
body: Oryn Thale is the Crusade made patient: iron, endurance, and the names chalked after the battle, not before. Doctrine, Iron doctrine: All ships gain +15% hull and +10% shields. Command, Iron wall: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round. Opens with Bastion-class battleship, Warden-class frigate. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend it at the start of the round you expect to be hit hardest, not after.

name: Line Admiral Oskar Maren
hook: Armored column: the fleet as a wall.
body: Oskar Maren is a column of armor with a flag on it, and the Registry projection for his battles is one word: favourable. Doctrine, Armored column: All ships gain +15% hull and +10% shields. Command, Shield wall order: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round. Opens with Dominion dreadnought, Hegemony picket. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend it at the start of the round you expect to be hit hardest, not after.

name: Nadir Aurex, Ninth Frame
hook: Endless restoration: the fleet rebuilds itself.
body: Nadir Aurex is on his ninth frame, and speaks of the previous eight the way other admirals speak of previous postings. Doctrine, Endless restoration: Ships regrow 4% of their hull each round. Command, Release the repair swarms: Every ship repairs 25% of its hull and patches damaged sections, even destroyed ones. Opens with Eclipse zenith, Eclipse flare. A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend it after the damage, not before: it patches even destroyed sections back into the fight.

name: Oath-Captain Malek Draven
hook: Hunter-killer: fast torpedoes, cruel rear arcs.
body: Malek Draven swore the oath as a boy in the Reach and hunts the way the Reach taught him: from behind, once. Doctrine, Hunter-killer: Torpedoes reload a turn faster, and rear-arc hits deal +50% damage. Command, Hunter's salvo: Torpedoes reload at once and every ship deals +30% damage this round. Opens with Harrow-class destroyer, Harrow-class destroyer, Warden-class frigate, Warden-class frigate. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend it on the round you have already lined up; the bonus does not carry to the next.

name: Old Mott
hook: Junkyard carriers: wings from welded dens.
body: Old Mott has outlived forty captains, mostly by killing them, and keeps his carriers welded, fed, and pointed at the fight. Doctrine, Junkyard carriers: Squadrons deal +25% damage, hulks hold +1 wing, and squadrons have +25% hull. Command, Release the swarm: Every carrier launches an extra wing, even past its hangar limit, then all squadrons strike again at once with +50% damage this round. Opens with Hullbreaker hulk-carrier, Hullbreaker gutship. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it when your wings are already out and in reach of targets worth striking twice.

name: Ostrel of the Long Copy
hook: Silent hunters: rear arcs and a low profile.
body: Ostrel of the Long Copy has been copied so often that the Archive keeps the original under guard. The copy hunts just fine. Doctrine, Silent hunters: +20% damage on rear-arc hits and +10 evasion. Command, Out of the shadow: Every ship deals +30% damage this round. Opens with Eclipse flare, Eclipse flare, Eclipse mote, Eclipse mote. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it on the round you have already lined up; the bonus does not carry to the next.

name: Razormaw
hook: Hunter pack: speed and rear-arc teeth.
body: Razormaw is the pack instinct of the swarm given a single throat: if it bleeds and it is slower than us, it is food. Doctrine, Hunter pack: +1 speed and +15% damage on rear-arc hits. Command, Blood frenzy: Every ship gains +2 movement and +1 turn, and enemy fire loses 20 accuracy against you this round. Opens with Chorus bladeback, Chorus spitter, Chorus drone-spawn. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend it to arrive a round early; position bought with the Command is position the enemy must answer.

name: Sable the Smiling Knife
hook: Knife work: rear arcs and criticals.
body: Sable the Smiling Knife hunts the way her namesake does: quiet, low, and finished before the noise starts. Doctrine, Knife work: +50% damage on rear-arc hits and +10% critical chance. Command, Knife in the dark: Torpedoes reload at once and every ship deals +30% damage this round. Opens with Hullbreaker gutship, Hullbreaker gutship, Hullbreaker raider, Hullbreaker raider. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend it on the round you have already lined up; the bonus does not carry to the next.

name: Saro of Long Focus
hook: Focused lances: beams with patience behind them.
body: Saro of Long Focus has waited out duels longer than most species live, and then fired once. Doctrine, Focused lances: Lances deal +20% damage and gain +10 aim. Command, Burning glass: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now. Opens with Glasswright prism, Glasswright lancet. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend the Command when the whole fleet can bear on targets; a volley fired at empty arcs is a volley lost.

name: Seveth, Twice-Restored
hook: Layered plates: hull, and then more hull.
body: Seveth has been restored twice, and has armored for a third death he does not intend to have. Doctrine, Layered plates: All ships gain +20% hull. Command, Sunshade wall: All shields refill and your ships take 40% less hull damage this round. Opens with Eclipse flare, Eclipse flare, Eclipse flare. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend it at the start of the round you expect to be hit hardest, not after.

name: Tamsa of the Clear Aperture
hook: Wing-mistress: carriers and wings, refined.
body: Tamsa of the Clear Aperture keeps her carriers the way her ancestors kept lenses: clean, aligned, and aimed at the light. Doctrine, Wing-mistress: Squadrons deal +25% damage, carriers hold +1 wing, and squadrons have +25% hull. Command, Starling flight: Every carrier launches an extra wing, even past its hangar limit, then all squadrons strike again at once with +50% damage this round. Opens with Glasswright aperture, Glasswright sliver. A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend it when your wings are already out and in reach of targets worth striking twice.

name: The Matriarch of Nine Throats
hook: Brood swarm: more swarms, hitting harder.
body: The Matriarch of Nine Throats is the swarm grown a general: nine mouths, and every one of them giving the same order. Eat. Doctrine, Brood swarm: Spore swarms deal +25% damage, broods hold +1 swarm, and squadrons have +25% hull. Command, Spawning surge: Every carrier launches an extra wing, even past its hangar limit, then all squadrons strike again at once with +50% damage this round. Opens with Chorus brood-sac, Chorus drone-spawn, Chorus drone-spawn. A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend it when your wings are already out and in reach of targets worth striking twice.

name: The Mending Throng
hook: Regrowth: the fleet knits itself closed.
body: The Mending Throng is the swarm remembering, through Memory, that flesh can be persuaded to close. Doctrine, Regrowth: Ships regrow 4% of their hull each round. Command, Regrowth tide: Every ship repairs 25% of its hull and patches damaged sections, even destroyed ones. Opens with Chorus bladeback, Chorus drone-spawn. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it after the damage, not before: it patches even destroyed sections back into the fight.

name: Umbra Vessane, Third-Housed
hook: Corona strikes: arcs first, everything second.
body: Umbra Vessane, third-housed, keeps her corona arcs the way Eclipse keeps everything: counted, cold, and ready. Doctrine, Corona strikes: Corona arcs deal +20% damage, and every weapon deals +10% more. Command, Noon volley: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now. Opens with Eclipse zenith, Eclipse mote, Eclipse mote. Unlocked with 30 renown.
note: Spend the Command when the whole fleet can bear on targets; a volley fired at empty arcs is a volley lost.

name: Vell of the Third Mirror
hook: Refraction tactics: nobody can hold a firing solution.
body: Vell of the Third Mirror fights in reflections: by the time you have found the real ship, it has moved twice. Doctrine, Refraction tactics: +8 evasion for every ship. Command, Scatter the light: Every ship gains +2 movement and +1 turn, and enemy fire loses 20 accuracy against you this round. Opens with Glasswright lancet, Glasswright lancet, Glasswright sliver, Glasswright sliver. Unlocked with 45 renown.
note: Spend it to arrive a round early; position bought with the Command is position the enemy must answer.

name: Vesh the Collector
hook: Scrap armor: the fleet patches itself.
body: Vesh the Collector takes ships apart to learn how they died, then wears the lesson as armor. Doctrine, Scrap armor: Ships patch 5% of their hull each round and have +10% armor. Command, Patch and weld: Every ship repairs 25% of its hull and patches damaged sections, even destroyed ones. Opens with Hullbreaker hulk-carrier, Hullbreaker gutship. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend it after the damage, not before: it patches even destroyed sections back into the fight.

name: Voice of the Deep
hook: Acid tide: every weapon bites harder.
body: Voice of the Deep is the throat that speaks first for the dark between stars, and what it says is usually a menu. Doctrine, Acid tide: +15% damage with every weapon. Command, Spitting volley: Every ship fires a free volley at the best target its guns can reach, right now. Opens with Chorus bladeback, Chorus spitter, Chorus drone-spawn. Unlocked with 80 renown.
note: Spend the Command when the whole fleet can bear on targets; a volley fired at empty arcs is a volley lost.

name: Warlord Grax Ironmaw
hook: Ram and board: speed and damage, pack style.
body: Grax Ironmaw earned the name the Hullbreaker way, in a challenge, and the pack has not questioned it since. Doctrine, Ram and board: +1 speed for every ship and +10% damage. Command, Full burn: Every ship gains +2 movement and +1 turn, and enemy fire loses 20 accuracy against you this round. Opens with Hullbreaker wrecker, Hullbreaker gutship, Hullbreaker gutship. A starting admiral, available from your first run.
note: Spend it to arrive a round early; position bought with the Command is position the enemy must answer.
source: data.js ADMIRALS.grax; faction Ashfall Hullbreakers; display name per text overhaul pack T-03 (Oct 27 rollout ruling)

name: Battleship hulls
hook: Battleship hulls join your shipyards.
body: Renown spent at the yards changes what the yards can build for you, on every run after. Effect: Battleship-class hulls appear in shipyards. Costs 60 renown, bought once, in the Shipyards line.

name: Carrier hulls
hook: Carrier hulls join your shipyards.
body: Renown spent at the yards changes what the yards can build for you, on every run after. Effect: Carrier hulls appear in shipyards. Costs 30 renown, bought once, in the Shipyards line.

name: Command authority I
hook: +2 fleet command points, every run.
body: Command authority is the paperwork of trust: more of the fleet answers to one plan. Effect: +2 fleet command points. Costs 35 renown, bought once, in the Command line.

name: Command authority II
hook: +2 more fleet command points, every run.
body: Wider command authority, earned the slow way, in fleets that came home. Effect: +2 more fleet command points. Costs 70 renown, bought once, in the Command line. Requires Command authority I first.

name: Dreadnought hulls
hook: One Daybreak dreadnought, for Crusade fleets.
body: The biggest permission the yards can give: a dreadnought of the Reach, one per fleet. Effect: Sunward Crusade fleets may take one Daybreak-class dreadnought. Costs 120 renown, bought once, in the Shipyards line. Requires Battleship hulls first.

name: Founders’ salvage
hook: Begin each run with a random piece of salvage.
body: The founders left a great deal lying around the dark; some of it still works. Effect: Begin each run with a random piece of salvage. Costs 60 renown, bought once, in the Supply line.

name: Master shipwrights
hook: Shipyard prices 15% lower, every run.
body: Master shipwrights do not charge less because they like you. They charge less because they waste nothing. Effect: Shipyard prices are 15% lower. Costs 45 renown, bought once, in the Supply line.

name: Recovery crews
hook: +20% credits from battles, every run.
body: Recovery crews are the difference between a wreck and a payday. Effect: +20% credits from battles. Costs 40 renown, bought once, in the Supply line.

name: Veteran officers
hook: Starting captains begin ranked and perked.
body: Veteran officers are what a fleet keeps when it cannot keep ships. Effect: Starting captains begin at Commander rank with a perk. Costs 50 renown, bought once, in the Command line.

name: War chest I
hook: +75 starting credits, every run.
body: A war chest is the fleet remembering to pack for the war it actually got. Effect: +75 starting credits. Costs 20 renown, bought once, in the Supply line.

name: War chest II
hook: +75 more starting credits, every run.
body: A deeper war chest, packed by people who have seen the first one run out. Effect: +75 more starting credits. Costs 40 renown, bought once, in the Supply line. Requires War chest I first.

name: War chest III
hook: +75 more starting credits, every run.
body: The deepest war chest: the difference between a plan and a hope, in credits. Effect: +75 more starting credits. Costs 65 renown, bought once, in the Supply line. Requires War chest II first.
